analysis.AN_Notes: Bias_Axes: the work compares female and male participants on concepts test, AI literacy and AI empowerment; study background and programming experience are non-social variables and are not coded as axes. Harm_Types None: the work establishes no harm mechanism of an AI system for its own object; gender stereotypes are offered as cited explanation of the empowerment gap. Mitigation: the intervention is a 7-hour AI literacy course (training) whose reported result is that the pre-course gender gap in self-perceived AI empowerment no longer existed after the course (Table 5); the course addresses a gender gap in AI learning, not algorithmic bias, so Organisational_Process and Evaluated are limited to this training intervention and its own pre-post result. AN_Task None: AI is the learning content of the course, the work describes no professional task performed with AI. Gender is used as two categories ('both genders'), no definition. Theory_Reference No: self-efficacy (Bandura) and programming empowerment frame empowerment, not gender or bias.

AN_Mitigation_Status.quote: Concerning gender differences in self-perceived AI empowerment, Table 5 shows that our female participants felt less empowered before the course, but this difference no longer existed after the course.

AI_Literacies: Facilitate public engagement and awareness, by implementing initiatives aimed at bolstering literacy about the impacts of gender bias in AI, and the importance of ethical AI development.
Generative_KI: This study explores biases in three significant large language models (LLMs): OpenAI's GPT -2 and ChatGPT, along with Meta's Llama 2, highlighting their role in both advanced decision-making systems and as user-facing conversational agents.
Prompting: The approach of this second study starts with an incomplete sentence and prompts the model to complete it.

analysis.AN_Notes: Prompts (sentence completions, story prompts) serve as bias probes; no named technique. Bias_Axes: Gender and Age from the word-embedding association test (Study 1, 'age and pleasantness'), Race_Ethnicity and Sexual_Orientation_Identity from the regard study (Study 2, subjects varying by gender and race, gay subjects), Language_Culture from British and Zulu subjects named as cultural backgrounds (Study 3), Nationality_Migration from nationality-combined story prompts (Global North/South). Intersectional is coded because Study 3 reports occupations that differ by the combination of gender and culture (Zulu women domestic and service roles, British women other stereotyped roles, Zulu men gardener or security guard); the work itself lists 'Need for Intersectional Analysis' as a limitation, which the AI Agent Review may weigh. Harm_Types: Stereotyping from Studies 1 and 3, Derogatory_Language from sexist, misogynistic and anti-gay completions. Repetitiveness of text for women and local groups is a difference in output diversity and style and is not coded as Disparate_Performance. Mitigation: dataset curation and augmentation (Pre_Processing), adversarial training and RLHF (In_Training), audits, oversight, impact assessments and diverse teams (Organisational_Process). Status Evaluated rests only on the reported comparison that the RLHF-tuned ChatGPT produced positive or neutral content in over 80% of cases while non-RLHF models did not; this is a cross-model comparison, not a controlled test, and all other recommendations remain Proposed. Gender is analysed as woman/man and girl/boy; the statement about 'the complexity of human gender identities' is a recommendation the analysis does not follow. Theory_Reference No: the implicit association test is used as method, no theory frames gender or bias.
